stem: The table gives the measures of two of the three angles of each of four triangles. Which two of the triangles must be similar to each other?
solution: Find each third angle with the \(180^{\circ}\) sum: I has \(70^{\circ}\), II has \(45^{\circ}\), III has \(75^{\circ}\), IV has \(50^{\circ}\).
Two triangles are similar when they have the same three angle measures (two matching pairs are enough).

Triangle I has angles \(45^{\circ}, 65^{\circ}, 70^{\circ}\) and triangle II has \(65^{\circ}, 70^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}\), the same set, so I and II are similar. No other pair shares two angle measures.

explanation.A: Incorrect. I and III share only the \(45^{\circ}\) angle; their other angles are \(65^{\circ}, 70^{\circ}\) and \(60^{\circ}, 75^{\circ}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. II and IV share only the \(70^{\circ}\) angle; comparing only the listed angles misses the third angle of each triangle.
explanation.C: Incorrect. III and IV share only the \(60^{\circ}\) angle; their third angles are \(75^{\circ}\) and \(50^{\circ}\).
explanation.D: Correct. Both triangles have angles of \(45^{\circ}\), \(65^{\circ}\), and \(70^{\circ}\).

verify:
rows={r[0]:[int(s.strip().rstrip('°')) for s in r[1].split(',')] for r in figure['rows']}
full={k:frozenset(v+[180-sum(v)]) for k,v in rows.items()}
assert full['I']==full['II']==frozenset({45,65,70})
names=['I','II','III','IV']
sim=[(p,q) for i,p in enumerate(names) for q in names[i+1:] if full[p]==full[q]]
assert sim==[('I','II')]
assert choices[answer]=='I and II'
